briefings.headline: Be ready for Houser’s fastball; make him finish the at-bat
briefings.message: Adrian Houser is the high-confidence predicted starter. Left-handed hitters have the clearest opening: be ready for his fastball-heavy mix, especially the sinker, but stay disciplined against the changeup and offspeed away. Right-handed hitters should look for their pitch and avoid chasing breaking balls. Brice Turang stays in the leadoff spot despite the rest suggestion. If a left-handed reliever enters late, Andrew Vaughn is the planned pinch-hit option; Christian Yelich is available against a right-hander.
reminders: Lefties: hunt a hittable fastball; don’t chase offspeed.
Make Houser prove he can finish at-bats.
Late matchup options: Vaughn versus a lefty, Yelich versus a righty.

briefings.headline: Crow sets the tone; attack the danger with a plan
briefings.message: Coleman Crow gets the start with a short leash: target 5.0 innings and cap him at 80 pitches. His season sample is small. Vary the cutter and curveball, and avoid predictable fastballs to Bryce Eldridge; his fastball xwOBA is 0.454, while his breaking-ball sample is small. Work carefully to Casey Schmitt—his offspeed xwOBA is 0.435, so it is not a clear weakness. If Crow’s command or contact worsens, turn to the rested leverage arms: Abner Uribe and Grant Anderson ahead of closer Trevor Megill. Shane Drohan is limited and best reserved for a one-batter need; Chad Patrick is unavailable.
reminders: Change eye level; don’t feed Eldridge predictable fastballs.
Be careful with Schmitt; offspeed is no clear weakness.
Use rested leverage arms if Crow falters; save Drohan for need only.
